calls.head: The Lightning will hunt a mismatch
calls.body: At home, the Lightning keep sending Goncalves’s line (Viel, Geekie and Goncalves) out against opponents’ fourth lines, far more often than chance would suggest. Jon Cooper has been chasing an easier matchup for the team’s scorers. Tonight the Blackhawks’ fourth line is Smith, Greene and Greenway.

calls.head: Expect the Lightning to have the puck more
calls.body: The Lightning have been one of the league’s best at controlling the chances at 5-on-5, and the Blackhawks one of the worst. Expect the Lightning to spend more of the night in the Blackhawks’ end. That’s about the puck, not the scoreboard: goalies and finishing decide plenty of games the chances don’t.

surprises.head: Chicago brought the hits
surprises.body: Chicago is one of the league’s lightest-hitting teams. Not tonight: a hit score of 184 in the close stretches of the game, against their usual 77 (100 is league average, adjusted for the arena’s scorer). A team strays this far about once every 225 games. That’s rarer than once a season for any one team.

story.head: Mikheyev scores against his old team
paras: Victor Hedman got the scoring started for the Lightning on the power play early in the first. Ilya Mikheyev stretched the lead to 2-0 late in the period, in his first game against Chicago since leaving. Dillon Boucher and Jeffrey Viel fought early in the second. Chicago had a goal taken off after a video review late in the period. Ryan McDonagh and Mikheyev scored two and a half minutes apart early in the third to make it 4-0. Roman Kantserov got the Blackhawks on the board with just under a minute left.

The Lightning had a bit more of the good stuff, outshooting the Blackhawks 35-26. Andrei Vasilevskiy made 25 saves for the Lightning, and Arvid Söderblom stopped 31 of 35 at the other end. By our Swing measure, Erik Černák had the best night of anyone. The Lightning improved to 10-3-2 and climbed to third in the Atlantic, while the Hawks fell to 4-12-1, still last in the Central.
